idea.title: The 1914 Christmas truce
idea.summary: On Christmas Eve 1914, enemy soldiers on the Western Front sang carols across the trenches and met in no man's land: strangers choosing to talk.
hookOptions: Soldiers stopped a war for Christmas
Enemies sang carols to each other in 1914
A war paused for a football game
sources: Wikipedia: Christmas truce: unofficial ceasefires along the Western Front around Christmas 1914.
Wikipedia: Christmas truce: German troops decorated trenches with candles and small Christmas trees; carols were sung and answered by the other side.
Wikipedia: Christmas truce: soldiers met in no man's land on Christmas Day, exchanged gifts, and football games were reported; the war then resumed.

scenes.say: Soldiers stopped a war to sing carols with the enemy.

scenes.caption: No man's land, 1914
scenes.say: It began on Christmas Eve, 1914, when German soldiers put little trees along their trenches.
They sang carols across the dark, and the British side sang back.
By Christmas morning, they were meeting in the middle, trading gifts, even kicking a ball.
The war went on after 1914, but for a while, enemies were just people talking.
